events.title: The Battle of Gravelines Breaks the Spanish Armada
events.description: English ships attacked the Spanish Armada off the coast of Gravelines, in present-day France. The Armada's formation was already scattered by fireships. Spain's fleet was driven into the North Sea and could no longer carry out its invasion plan.
events.significance: The defeat protected Elizabethan England from invasion. It also marked a turning point in European naval power.

events.title: Edison Patents the Mimeograph
events.description: Thomas Edison received a patent for the mimeograph. The machine made many copies of a document from a stencil. Offices, schools and churches soon adopted it.
events.significance: It made duplicating documents cheap and easy, and it was a forerunner of the modern photocopier.

events.title: The Battle of Amiens Begins
events.description: Allied forces launched a surprise attack near Amiens in northern France. They used tanks, aircraft and coordinated infantry and artillery. The German army suffered heavy losses in the opening hours.
events.significance: The attack opened the Hundred Days Offensive, which led to the end of World War I a few months later.

events.title: The Great Train Robbery
events.description: A gang of 15 robbers stopped a Royal Mail train at Bridego Railway Bridge in Buckinghamshire, England. They took about £2.6 million in banknotes. It was one of the largest robberies in British history.
events.significance: The audacious heist gripped the public, led to a huge police manhunt and became a lasting part of British popular culture.
